synthesis.body: A plan that specifies more test mechanism than an implementer needs generates its own review findings. Across five spec-stage review rounds on install-to-ship-walkthrough the sustained counts fell 26, 10, 8, 4, 1 -- but 6 of the 10 in round 2 and 6 of the 8 in round 3 were defects introduced by the previous round's repairs, not by the original draft. Each of those rounds converged only when the repair REMOVED a claim: a two-altitude source-plus-rendered check design collapsed to rendered-only, a browser-gate visibility claim was withdrawn to a stated accepted gap, and a scalar route count became a committed route set. new-spec already names the rule -- when a reviewer keeps finding under-specification in the plan rather than defects in the spec, the plan is over-specified: reduce it, do not extend it. Make the ratio visible: tag every finding draft-origin or prior-round-repair, and treat any round whose findings are majority prior-round-repair as the signal to cut. Under that discipline the follow-on slice was drafted at 4 criteria and 3 tasks rather than 14 and 5.

title: A review round whose findings are mostly prior-round repairs is the signal to cut the plan, not extend it
